description: A 6 member team from the University of Information Technology Myanmar
summary:
Anyar is a bilingual farming decision-support web application designed for Myanmar’s Central Dry Zone, with an initial focus on Magway. It helps farmers map their fields, understand NASA environmental data, and explore crop rotations that fit their seasons, water availability, and priorities.

Developed for Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data, Anyar brings NASA POWER weather and soil-wetness estimates, GPM IMERG rainfall, and MODIS imagery together with local crop calendars and farmer-provided information. Users can compare their usual plan with alternatives, explore seasonal scenarios, review market context, and ask an AI agriculture advisor questions in Burmese or English.

Our goal is to make space-based information understandable and useful for everyday farm decisions. By showing sources, uncertainty, and practical checks alongside planning options, Anyar supports informed choices that could conserve water, protect soil, and strengthen farming resilience. It is an exploratory prototype that supports farmers’ judgment and local expertise.
details:
What exactly does it do

  • Draw & save a field — Leaflet map over Esri World Imagery / OpenStreetMap basemaps; Turf.js computes boundary area and centroid; fields persist in browser localStorage (fieldshift-magway.v1), so no account is needed.
  • NASA weather context — for the field centroid only (the boundary is never uploaded): monthly T2M + PRECTOTCORR (2016–present, community AG), daily GPM IMERG_PRECTOT rainfall (last three complete months), a 25-year monthly climatology, and daily GWETTOP / GWETROOT / ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN soil-wetness screening. Shown as "recent months vs historical reference" charts with grid-cell resolution (~0.5° × 0.625°), retrieval date, provenance, and explicit cached / demo-snapshot / unavailable states.
  • Satellite history — a dated NASA GIBS MODIS Terra true-colour imagery slider over the field.
  • Explore Myanmar in 3D — a Three.js extruded atlas of 14 ADM1 regions (geoBoundaries) coloured by NASA POWER 2001–2025 monthly climatology (rainfall, temperature, root-zone wetness), with month/layer controls, bilingual region names, and an explicit "unsupported region" notice everywhere except Magway so no planning data is invented.
  • Crop planning — six supported crops (sesame, groundnut, green/black gram, chickpea, pigeon pea), FAO crop-calendar-based rotation recommendations, scenario editor, comparison of next-season and two-year what-ifs, next-calendar-year recommendations with planting/harvest windows, saved fields, a 2D timeline and an illustrative 3D seasonal view.
  • Crop prices — real WFP Myanmar retail price observations (2008–2026, normalised MMK/kg → MMK/tonne), filterable by crop/region/unit, with source and method disclosures.
  • AI Agriculture Advisor — public, no sign-in, in-memory streaming chat in Myanmar or English; accepts plant photos; uses farm context; calls farmObservations (NASA POWER), officialSources (domain-allowlisted DOA/DMH search) and greenwaySources (Green Way articles) and returns clickable dated citations.
  • Crop/fruit picture search — Wikipedia/Wikimedia API with a Myanmar-name dictionary, kept separate from modelled crops so unmodelled plants never receive invented scores.
  • A 30-second demo video — real screen-recorded app footage, English narration, burned-in captions, storyboard and verification report.

How it works

Next.js App Router renders the UI; browser-only Leaflet, Three.js and Recharts are lazy-loaded behind client-only boundaries for SSR/mobile performance. A getNasaClimate() service builds NASA POWER point-API URLs from the field centroid, requests monthly + IMERG daily data in parallel, validates responses (rejecting fill sentinels), caches them for 12 h, and falls back gracefully to cached data or a bundled, dated real snapshot on rate-limit/network failure. Rotation and recommendation engines use deterministic local rules plus FAO calendars; they never convert NASA data into a crop-suitability score. The advisor is a server route handler (/api/public/advisor) that streams an AI model response with validated, size-capped input and tool calls to Parallel Search/Extract; an optional Supabase switch only gates availability. All keys stay server-side. Every dataset is displayed with its retrieval date, resolution and limitations ("area-level model estimate, not a field sensor, not a forecast, not SMAP").

Benefits

Privacy-first (no sign-in, boundary stays local), fully bilingual, mobile-first, works offline-ish via cached snapshots, honest about uncertainty (missing data = "unknown", never "no warnings"), accessible in both languages, and safe by design (no invented pesticide doses, diagnoses or official warnings). It turns abstract satellite archives into concrete "next checks" a farmer can verify by hand.

What we hope to achieve

A practical decision aid farmers can trust — helping them choose crops confidently, protect soil, and build climate resilience — and a reusable, transparent pattern for bringing NASA Earth data to low-connectivity, smallholder contexts. Longer term: validate with local agronomists and farmer cooperatives, add more supported regions/crops only when real data exists, and keep every claim traceable to a dated source.

Tools, languages, hardware, software

TypeScript / JavaScript, React 19, Next.js 16 (App Router), Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui + Radix, Leaflet, Turf.js, Three.js / React Three Fiber / drei, Recharts, Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk), Zod, Drizzle/Supabase (optional), Vitest + Testing Library, ESLint/Prettier, Node ≥20.9, npm/bun, deployed on Vercel. Video pipeline: Python 3, Pillow, NumPy, imageio-ffmpeg/FFmpeg, Playwright, edge-tts, HeyGen (cloud TTS/music). Hardware: a standard Windows laptop/desktop and a modern web browser; no custom hardware, sensors or IoT devices.
